summary: Iron tower on a concrete pier off eastern Lake Ontario, first built at Vermilion, Ohio, in 1877 and set on this shoal in 1935; never staffed.

lens.where: Coast Guard base, Buffalo, New York

structures.note: Built for Vermilion, Ohio; installed on this shoal in 1935 (USLHS: moved from storage).

structures.material: stone-filled timber crib with concrete superstructure
structures.note: Crib 50 ft square; deckhouse and riprap added.

access.note: Privately owned since 2009; tower closed to visitors.

events.note: Octagonal iron tower first installed at Vermilion, Ohio, at the end of a pier
Buoy on the main Charity Shoal replaced by a gas buoy (since 1 July 1897, per the Light-House Board annual report for fiscal 1897, printed p. 162)

Station established, per USLHS place record; no light described for that year
Temporary light on a pole on the south side of the crib, 24 November 1934; lighted buoy discontinued
Crib, concrete superstructure and octagonal iron tower completed; 14 ft of water
Fourth-order fixed lens (Bulletin, LighthouseFriends); USLHS record says fifth order
Rosedale stranded on East Charity Shoal in a northwest gale
Rock Ferry aground on the shoal; tugs sent to free her
Physician washed overboard; reached the pier after more than eight hours; picked up next morning by three fishermen

Online auction; sold 27 August 2009 for $25,501 to a private buyer

corrections.why: USLHS place record gives the height from base of structure to centre of lantern as 16 ft (4.9 m); the record says 12.0 m.
LighthouseFriends dates the first light on the shoal (a temporary light on a pole) to 24 November 1934. The USLHS 1929 date is an establishment year with no light described.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record notes that sources give different first years. The tower was first built at Vermilion in 1877 (LighthouseFriends). The USLHS record gives 1929 as the year the station was established. A temporary light on a pole was lit on 24 November 1934 (LighthouseFriends). The permanent tower and crib were completed in 1935 (Bulletin, USLHS). The story gives each date with its source.

The USLHS record gives a fifth-order Fresnel lens. The 1935 Bulletin and LighthouseFriends give fourth order. The story follows the Bulletin and LighthouseFriends and notes the USLHS entry as unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Revised 2026-10-27 by the independent fact-check. Changes: the buoy on Charity Shoal was replaced by a gas buoy 'since July 1, 1897' per the FY1897 Light-House Board report (the record and the first draft said 1896); the story no longer says the Board's 1896-97 report 'lists' the buoy without a date. Printed pages for the Light-House Board volumes were read from the OCR running heads (FY1901 buoyage: p. 172; FY1897 Tenth District note: p. 162); the volumes have no scan-page index here, so the page images were not viewed. The Bulletin (1935 PDF p. 29) was checked against the cached text: 'composed of a stone-filled timber crib', 'a fourth order lantern', 'candlepower of 1,300', 'The station is unattended.' The Tribune item (11 Dec 1897 p. 4) was read directly: 'Kingston, Ont, Dec. 10' and 'have stripped the vessel and abandoned her'. The USLHS keeper roster link (showPeople/3405) printed no names when read; roster.py also reports none listed. The place record says 'Private Aid: No' while LighthouseFriends says the lighthouse is privately owned and the story now says the record lists it as an active aid, not a private one; the conflict is not resolved. The record's 'Original Optic Type: FIFTH ORDER, FRESNEL' conflicts with the 1935 Bulletin and LighthouseFriends (fourth order); left open. The 1937 profile ('Olin Stevens Tends Beacon') is known only as LighthouseFriends quotes it; its newspaper is not named there and the paper was not identified. The 1955 account is known only through LighthouseFriends (Oswego Palladium-Times, 6 Aug 1955, not read). Named private individuals: Dr. Joseph G. Reidel (1955 rescue, not a keeper or service member) is named as the published sources name him; the 1955 buyer and later owners are not named. The Olin W. Stevens connection to this station is not established: the 1937 article ties him to the Vermilion tower and to Tibbetts Point; the story says the passage does not place him on the shoal. LighthouseFriends is a copyrighted site: the story paraphrases it and keeps only one short quoted phrase ('an old friend') from the 1937 article as LighthouseFriends quotes it. The record's characteristic 'Fl W 4s' and the Wikipedia 'Fl R 4s' were not used and remain unverified; the NRHP 2008 listing claim is unverified (the record's nomination copy is a placeholder).
